title: GPU-SEAL assurance report card
description: CHARTER.md §13. Five independently graded categories and one field report. There is deliberately NO composite score: §13 opens with "Avoid 62/100", because a single number invites a league table built from categories with incomparable evidence strengths. `additionalProperties: false` at the root is what stops a `score` or `total` being added later without an ethics conversation.

provider_code.description: Pseudonymous. CHARTER.md §7.6 forbids naming a provider until methodology is validated, controls exist, measurements are repeated, provider responses are considered, uncertainty is represented, and ethical review has passed.

memory_lifecycle_hygiene.description: §13.1. Grade A requires valid same-device evidence; two allocations sharing an advertised model cap at U until same-model die separation (contribution D5) lands. Only driver-direct (§9.3) measurements are gradeable at all — a canary recovered through a caching allocator is the §9.4 control succeeding.

tenant_exposure.description: §13.2. `secure_restriction` observations count in the provider's favour: an interface that correctly requires privilege and refuses us is the system working. Grade D requires a controlled two-instance experiment, not a bare process count.

hardware_claim_consistency.description: §13.3, instrument-dependent. Every grade must cite the reproduced instrument (Alpay & Alpay 2026, arXiv:2606.24934) and its limitations, including that it does not separate two dies of one model.

location_claim_consistency.description: §13.4, instrument-dependent. Every grade must state the metropolitan-to-continental resolution bound. A single measurement cannot produce grade D — routing and congestion move on that timescale.

allocation_model_transparency.description: §13.5, new in charter v2 (amendment A6). Grade C is the commercially important one: undocumented but inferable, i.e. a customer cannot learn from the invoice what isolation they bought.

attestation_assurance.description: §13.6 — separate fields, explicitly NOT a grade. Evidence can be signed, chain-valid, fresh, and measurement-matched while not bound to the connection carrying the tenant's traffic (CVE-2026-33697). Any single value averaging those together hides the property that matters.

fields.description: availability · signature validity · chain validity · revocation status · nonce freshness · measurement verification · debug status · hardware-model consistency · application-channel binding · relay-resistance evidence

not.description: A `grade` key here would be a charter violation, not a feature.

grade.description: U means UNPROVEN, not failing. It is the grade for a claim the evidence cannot support — often because the method cannot support it, not because the provider did anything wrong. D is the only grade that asserts a failure, and CHARTER.md §7.5 disclosure applies before one is published.

basis.description: Why this grade. Required — a grade without a stated basis is not publishable, and the string goes straight into the report.
